latest_release.name: TensorFold 1.3.5
latest_release.body:
# TensorFold 1.3.5

1.3.5 adds TFQ3, TensorFold's own quantized weight format, for GLM-5.3-Flash and Flash Next on Metal, and brings Inkling 2 Mini to native serving on CUDA and Metal, with images on Metal and large decode speedups on both. New models and paths include SenseNova-Loop-9B on Metal, Ripple-65B-Preview on CUDA, speech input for Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, ZONOS3 Mini text to speech and Idol end to end on M5. The contributing rules now say exactness is bit for bit: a changed reduction order or rounding point must keep every output bit, by default and with any switch on (#4888).

## TFQ3

TFQ3 is TensorFold's own quantized weight format: `.tffpw` record files and a shared `pw_v3_tables.bin` beside a checkpoint, loaded zero-copy and run by native Metal kernels. A checkpoint without TFQ3 records takes the same paths as before. Within TFQ3, a repeat equals its prefill and 1-row decode equals multi-row decode, while prompt and decode may differ in the last bits.

- **GLM on Metal:** TFQ3 weight loading (`layer_XX.tffpw`, `nonmoe.tffpw`, `pw_v3_tables.bin`) with decode and prefill kernels for M5 and earlier Macs, plus 8-bit/64 KDA split-parts and window kernels. On an M5 Ultra, `GLM-5.3-Flash-TFQ3` (`139.55 GB` on disk) loads in 8.4 s, matches `depth 0 == depth 3` bit-identically, prefills `p2048` at 1,567 tok/s and decodes at 69.2 tok/s (`B=1`), 87-104 tok/s with live MTP streaming. Non-TFQ3 checkpoints compile no TFQ3 kernels (#4953).
- **Flash Next on Metal:** checkpoints with TFQ3 routed MoE sidecars (`pw_v3_tables.bin`, `layer_XX.tffpw`, `mtp_00.tffpw`) run native TFQ3 kernels for decode (`B=1` and deduplicated `B=2..16`) and prompt prefill; non-TFQ3 checkpoints stay on the existing MLX affine paths. `--ple-on-ssd` works with TFQ3 and an incompatible `--ssd-experts` is refused. On an M5 Ultra, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-TFQ3` (78.99 GiB) reaches 5.996 combined PPL (against 6.007 for the 8-bit source and 6.644 for MLX 4-bit), 3,855 tok/s `p2048` prefill, 82.9 tok/s `B=1` decode and 154.5 tok/s at `MTP depth=3`, with bit-exact `depth 0 == depth 3` parity (#4964).
- **Release fixes:** GLM decode windows of 8 to 16 rows give each row the same bytes as 1-row decode (the prompt pass alone uses the MMA kernels), GLM refuses misaligned 4-bit records, a stray `pw_v3_tables.bin` no longer turns TFQ3 on for a checkpoint without TFQ3 records (GLM and Flash Next), and Flash Next checks its table file as GLM does (#4996).

## Speed

- **Inkling 2 Mini on Metal:** routed experts and the combine run a thread per output with the same serial arithmetic, so one-stream decode is about 16x faster on an M5 Ultra and 17x on an M3 Ultra (#4894). The router's and loop gates' dots do the same, so prompts reach the first token about 42% sooner and four streams decode about 64% faster on an M5 Ultra (#4912). DSpark drafting uses the 1/sqrt(128) attention scale and reads kappa as FP32, so one-stream draft acceptance on an M3 Ultra rises from 3% to 55% and drafted decode is about 56% faster (#4447). Tokens and replies are unchanged in each.
- **Inkling 2 Mini on CUDA:** expert weights staged a warp at a time make one-stream decode about 70% faster on GB10, four streams about 60% faster and long prompts reach the first token about 25% sooner (#4728); the loop gate as a down and an up half adds about 28% one-stream (#4697), and decode experts a warp over 8 columns about 3% more (#4729). Tokens are identical.
- **Lanes (host sampler):** Flint, Llama, Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3's draws keep a draw's best 1,024 candidates in one bounded heap pass instead of sorting the row, bit for bit the full sort's. On an M4 Pro a sampled stream of a 201,058-token-vocabulary model decodes at 29.2 tokens a second where it did 21.2, and four streams at 56.1 where 33.5; greedy is unchanged (#4744).
- **GLM on Metal:** one-Mac GLM-5.3-Flash prefills short remaining work first by default, cutting a short reply beside a long prompt from 6.11 s to 3.56 s with long-prompt TTFT within 1

Help Support TensorFold · @tensorfold_dev on X

# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-with-agents). ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, a small 4-bit checkpoint. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). The [run guide](docs/run-guide.md#platform-setup) lists the archive's requirements; Windows has [its own guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). ```sh V=1.3.5 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. To talk to a model in the terminal in one command, `tensorfold chat MODEL` starts the server itself, streams each reply and stops the server when the chat ends; `/help` lists the chat's commands, and `/bye` or Ctrl-D ends it: ```sh tensorfold chat mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit ``` With the server above still running, `tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` chats with it instead, and `echo "Say hello." | tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` prints one reply for a script. See [the chat command](docs/chat.md) for its flags and the serve flags it passes on. ## Docs - [Run guide](docs/run-guide.md): platform setup, requests, parallel requests, exact decoding, context compaction, Cortheon mode, every serve flag, the Mac app and TensorFold Starlight. - [Supported models](docs/supported-models.md): which checkpoints run on which machines, models on disk and model discovery. - [Living Weights (experimental)](docs/living-weights.md): teach a running model new facts in its own weights. - [Installation runbook](RUNBOOK.md): macOS and CUDA installation, paired Metal serving and troubleshooting. - [Windows](docs/WINDOWS.md), [TensorFold Web](docs/web.md) and [the Mac app](app/README.md). - [API](docs/api.md), [Cortheon mode](docs/cortheon.md) and [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). - [Claude Code](docs/claude-code.md): point it at a local server, name its model, and keep its prompt prefix cacheable. - [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) and [community benchmarks](docs/community-benchmarks.md). - [Usable memory profiles](docs/memory-profiling.md): how to record applied budgets, context, cache state and process peaks. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): ATC and agents, builds, tests and the exactness and performance gates. - [Changes](CHANGELOG.md), [1.0.0 release notes](docs/release-notes-1.0.0.md) and [the Zig engine preview](docs/zig-preview.md). - TensorFold is Apache-2.0: [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Contributors
